title: Lum and Abner
paragraphs: A long-running rural comedy centered on Lum Edwards and Abner Peabody, proprietors of the Jot 'Em Down Store in the fictional community of Pine Ridge, Arkansas.

Long-running rural comedy created and performed by Chester Lauck and Norris Goff. Most of the run used a short serialized strip centered on the Jot Em Down Store in Pine Ridge, with a documented 1948-1950 half-hour comedy-variety detour before returning to short-form episodes.

GRH documents the program through Mutual serial era (April 2, 1934 to August 30, 1935) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], Blue Network serial era (September 2, 1935 to February 25, 1938) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], CBS serial era (February 28, 1938 to March 29, 1940) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and NBC Pacific serial era (May 26, 1941 to September 19, 1941) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|chester-lauck|Chester Lauck]] (performer on 652 recordings), [[person|norris-goff|Norris Goff]] (performer on 651 recordings), Lou Crosby (announcer on 331 recordings and performer on 1 recording), Carlton Brickert (announcer on 81 recordings), Clarence Hartzell (performer on 24 recordings), Gene Baker (announcer on 21 recordings), and Barbara Stanwyck (performer on 2 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network), and [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Waters, Arkansas renamed Pine Ridge in honor of Lum and Abner, Lum and Abner during the World War II home front, and Lum and Abner during radio format and television-era change.
